transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-14 15:00 PT - 46 minutes
Attendees: Laura Kim, Rafael Ortiz, Priya Shah (Redwood) | Ethan Park, Maya Lin, Samir Patel (NovaEdge)
---
Summary: quick sync on marketplace listing flow and reference arch for private deployments; action items captured below.
---
00:00 Laura: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Laura from Redwood here, i got Rafael our solutions engineer and Priya on the line. Howre you folks doing?
00:18 Ethan: Doing good, thanks. Maya and Samir here. We sent over the initial marketplace form earlier this week, looking to confirm technical bits.
00:30 Laura: Yep we saw that, thanks. Today we want to align on the listing fields, reference architecture for Redwood Private integrations, and a test plan for provisioning and metering. Rafael, want to kick off on arch?
00:52 Rafael: Sure, yeah. So high level, we treat the marketplace listing as two parts, the consumer facing listing and the backend provisioning integration. For private deployments we typically recommend a reference arch where NovaEdge preps a VPC peering or transit gateway and we support a customer-managed network with a small control plane in our partner region.
01:20 Maya: sorry can you repeat transit gateway bit, i missed that part.
01:24 Rafael: yeah so what i mean is if NovaEdge wants Redwood Private to be discoverable from the marketplace, you can either do a direct SaaS integration where we provision a tenant in our hosted control plane, or for a private offering we support a bring-your-own VPC model. In the bring-your-own model we do an encrypted tunnel and optional VPC peering - depends on your networking constraints.
02:01 Samir: And for billing, does the marketplace handle metering and pass back usage to Redwood, or do we need to forward receipts?
02:12 Priya: Good question. For AWS/GCP marketplace there's a metering API flow - typically the marketplace reports usage and we reconcile. For CloudMart-like partner marketplaces there are two options, either using marketplace metering or letting NovaEdge capture payment and call our billing API. We should document both.
02:45 Ethan: On SSO, our customers expect SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. Where does that land in the architecture?
02:55 Rafael: We support SAML and OIDC as the identity bridge. For NovaEdge marketplace customers we can accept SAML assertions from your IdP and map groups to RBAC in Redwood Console. SCIM provisioning is supported for user sync. We'll include the SSO handshake sequence in the reference diagram.
03:25 Maya: Is KMS integration possible for customers who want their own keys?
03:30 Rafael: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. In the reference arch we show an optional KMS endpoint on the customer side and key wrapping. Note that for hosted marketplace listings that provision hosted tenants, customers can also bring keys via a dedicated key envelope flow, but that's more advanced.
04:02 Laura: Good, i want to also call out model variants and deployment options - some customers will want Dedicated reserved capacity instead of Private. That affects quota and SLA fields in the listing.
04:22 Samir: ok so on the marketplace form there are fields for pricing and plan types; we'll map those to Dedicated vs Private.
04:28 Priya: yes exactly, we should list feature gates: dedicated, private (vpc), hosted. Also call out performance expectations (latency SLO) for Dedicated vs Hosted.
04:48 Ethan: On the provisioning API, whats the sequence? create tenant, exchange secrets, setup network, verify health?
05:00 Rafael: roughly: 1) partner sends create-tenant request to Redwood provisioning endpoint with partner auth, 2) we return a provisioning token, 3) partner calls back with network/topology details, 4) we initiate setup, exchange certs, and run health checks. We'll provide a sample OpenAPI snippet.
05:35 Maya: awesome. For the testing plan, can Redwood run a lab test where we provision a test tenant from the marketplace UI?
05:42 Laura: yes we can do a staging end-to-end. Rafael, can you coordinate the staging test?
05:49 Rafael: Yep i'll set up a staging tenant and a script that exercises create-tenant, sso login, model call, and metering ping. We prefer to run it in the week of May 25th, sounds good?
06:05 Ethan: Works for us, we'll provide a staging account.
06:10 Samir: Quick question on security docs - NovaEdge legal needs SOC2 and data residency notes to appear in the listing. Do you have a standard blurb?
06:22 Priya: We have SOC 2 type II and an ISO statement in our security pack. We'll share a security brief and an audit log example. For data residency we'll document region limitations and whether logs cross borders.
06:40 Maya: There was some noise in the marketplace requirements where customer data retention fields are required, can you confirm default retention?
06:48 Rafael: Default logs retention is 30 days in the console, but for Private you can set longer retention in config. We'll include that.
07:00 Laura: On reference arch diagram, Rafael will include networking, SSO, KMS, and metering. Also call out fallback routing - if Dedicated not available fall back to hosted with rate limits.
07:18 Ethan: Fallback is important for enterprise customers. How do we control model variants?
07:25 Rafael: We can present a policy layer in the diagram: route by customer tier, latency budget, and fallback to lighter quantized model. We'll show that as a control plane policy.
07:44 Maya: About marketplace assets, what format do you need for logos and screenshots?
07:49 Priya: We need svg/png at 1200x600 for hero, 512x512 for thumbnails, a 1-page PDF, and a short 200-300 word product blurb. We'll send the checklist.
08:05 Samir: On legal side, any standard terms we should expect to include for the listing?
08:11 Laura: We'll provide a partner addendum template; NovaEdge legal can redline. Also include support SLAs for Dedicated customers and support contact.
08:25 Ethan: Good. For the reference arch doc, do you have a sample from a previous partner?
08:30 Rafael: Yes i can share a reference architecture we used with CloudMart - i'll scrub customer names and share. Expect that by 2026-05-21.
08:42 Maya: Perf testing: will you run token throughput tests? We want to validate qps on a 4xA100 cluster.
08:52 Rafael: We can run perf tests in staging, but note that quantization and batch sizes affect throughput. We'll propose a benchmark script that measures p95 latency at different seq lengths.
09:10 Samir: Can we configure model quantization at the tenant level?
09:14 Rafael: Yes, model and quantization profiles can be part of the tenant config for Private and Dedicated. We'll note recommended defaults for chat vs embedding workloads.
09:28 Maya: Also need an integration for billing ids so marketplace order maps to our internal plan codes.
09:34 Priya: We'll add a mapping table in the listing checklist: marketplace_plan_id -> internal_plan_code -> Redwood billing sku.
09:45 Ethan: Any blockers for go-live timeline if we want listing live by June 15th?
09:52 Laura: It is tight but doable if we hit the asset and tech deliverables. Key dependencies are: reference arch, staging test success, legal sign-off, and marketplace approvals.
10:10 Samir: ok let us prioritize assets and legal.
10:14 Maya: are there any API quotas defaulted? We need to know rate limits for the marketplace plan.
10:21 Rafael: Default rate limits for hosted tenants are 60 rps with burst; Dedicated is configurable per commit. We'll include the exact headers and retry guidance in the API doc.
10:40 Ethan: For the staging test - what telemetry will you collect?
10:45 Rafael: We'll collect provisioning logs, SSO success rates, model latency (p50/p90/p95), error rates, and metering pings. We'll share a dashboard link in Console once tests run.
11:05 Maya: will you share the OpenAPI for provisioning?
11:08 Rafael: Yes, will post a swagger/openapi file to the shared repo.
11:12 Laura: Ok let's capture next steps quickly.
11:20 Ethan: quick clarification, if a customer uses their own KMS, does NovaEdge or Redwood manage key rotation?
11:28 Rafael: Key rotation remains customer responsibility for customer-managed keys; we support automatic rotation hooks if you push new key material. We'll document the flow.
11:45 Priya: action items are in the meeting notes.
11:50 Laura: Great thanks everyone. We'll send notes and schedule the staging window.
11:56 Samir: Thanks folks, talk soon.
12:00 END
